leanMin.citation: CES ideo5 'very liberal' on the -2 to +2 lean scale (ces-2024-views.json).

leanMax.citation: CES ideo5 'very conservative' on the -2 to +2 lean scale (ces-2024-views.json).

hashDigits.citation: Hex digits of a stable hash read as one uniform value.

minimumCellRespondents.citation: A state-by-age cell with fewer CES respondents falls back to the whole state. Checked by towns staying inside their state's spread; spread 20 to 100.

householdShare.citation: Share of a person's opening lean that their household shares. Parent-child correlations of political orientation run about 0.4 to 0.6 (Jennings, Stoker and Bowers 2009, Journal of Politics 71(3):782-799), and spouses correlate about 0.6 on ideology (Alford, Hatemi, Hibbing, Martin and Eaves 2011, Journal of Politics 73(2):362-379).
householdShare.estimatedFrom: Jennings, Stoker and Bowers 2009; Alford et al. 2011; spread 0.4 to 0.6

tightness.citation: How much less an engaged person's stance moves on one event: people who follow politics closely resist new messages more (Zaller 1992, The Nature and Origins of Mass Opinion). No study sets the size; spread 0.25 to 0.75.

stanceStep.citation: How far one event that reaches a person moves their stance on its topic, per unit of the event's appraised impulse. No study sets the size; checked by a big event moving the people it touched and no one else. Spread 0.05 to 0.2.

partyHouseholdShare.citation: The share of people whose party reads their household's draw rather than their own, so members of one home share a party more often than chance: about 70% of married couples share a party registration and about 30% are mismatched, independents included (Hersh and Ghitza 2018, PLOS ONE 13(10):e0203997).

speechLeanPull.citation: How far one speech heard moves a listener's lean toward the speaker's, before nearness and how loosely they hold their views. Persuasion effects of a single campaign contact are small and often near zero (Kalla and Broockman 2018, American Political Science Review 112(1):148-166); a starting value.

partyStickiness:strong.citation: What holds a strong partisan to their party point against a lean that has moved nearer the next point's average. Party identification is the stablest political attitude; about 8 in 10 registered voters gave the same answer in all five waves from 2018 to 2020, and 9% of each party moved to the other (Pew Research Center, 'Voters Rarely Switch Parties', Aug 4, 2020).

partyStickiness:weak.citation: What holds a weak partisan to their party point; looser than a strong partisan (Pew Research Center 2020, as for the strong).

partyStickiness:lean.citation: What holds a leaner to their point; the loosest attachment (Pew Research Center 2020).

partyStickiness:independent.citation: What holds an independent at the middle of the scale (Pew Research Center 2020).
